en: Having prostrated before Gaṇeśa for the removal of doubts, I shall expound the Śikṣā, which is the fundamental cause of the Vedas. (1)

In the *vṛjana* [intonation], if the acute (*udātta*) syllable is uttered together with the vowel *a*, that word is called *stuta*; however, at the end of a sentence, it is proclaimed as *pracaya*. (2)
Up to the fifth [syllable], it is preceded by *havya* and offered with clarified butter (*ghṛta*) while held upwards;
likewise, that which is at the end of a sentence is also so described, provided that no other [such word] exists before it. (3)
The *paraśu* (axe) is prescribed for the *antodātta* (acute-accented at the end); the *parśu* is [prescribed] by way of division (*bhaktitā*).
The *parṣad* here is also the *atiparṣad*; however, the accentual division (*svarabhakti*) is constant.

One should understand that the *svarabhakti* occurs when a vowel follows a *pāpa* (anusvāra) or a *viloma* (visarga), as well as in the cases beginning with "kārṣīt"; no other consonant can occur in this position.
O Agni, Lord of Food, [recite] the three [verses] with the Triṣṭubh meter; thus it should be from this point onward.
In the Kaṭhaka [school], there are also the Kṣiprā, Bhartrya, Ayitrya, Arātrya, Mantrya, and Pitrya [sections].
But when they are in the same word, those which are short, long, and protracted are [respectively] *juṣṭaḥ*, *vācaḥ*, *prajāgnim*, *ciṃmānaḥ*, *mitraḥ*, and *udastaḥ*. || 7 ||
Agni indeed is the one who causes the shaving of the hair for the gods;
for in the Anuvākas beginning with "rakṣāṃsi," he likewise becomes possessed of the vowel 'ī'.

O Agni, that which is your desire for the sacrificial grass and the kindling, O Great One, as well as the beginning with the word "tvikāra" for the first sacrifice of the ritual, has been proclaimed. || 9 ||
If [the vowel] were *akāriṣam*, *caṇaḥ*, *pūrvaḥ*, *rīriṣaḥ*, *rīriṣan*, *api*, *tāriṣat*, *ca*, *ariṣam*, and *cet*, then the *svarabhakti* would not be found. (10)
In the section on prepositions (*upasarga*) beginning with "iyuri," there exists [the rule]; from the *Juṣṭapraśna* section, the *mānuṣī* recitation occurs in the *Chidrāraṇyaka*. 11.
In the case of *viniṣparyasuraḥpūrvakrīyā*, those [suffixes] do not follow;
in *cātūrathasya*, the first two [suffixes] are applied, as well as the *hotrī* and *maptrī* suffixes, which have long vowels.
potrī, neṣṭrī, svasrī, stotrī, śatarudrī, and naṇām paraḥ;
also varīyasī, pīyūṣaḥ, davīyaḥ, and hrasīyaḥ. || 13 ||
The second is accumulated, and likewise the third and those following;
however, the non-third is drunk away, and those who are not wolves go upward.
But when preceded by a vowel and followed by *ś*, *ṣ*, or *h*, the *ṛ* sound situated between them becomes the vowel *u*; thus, there is no *svarabhakti*. (15)
If *rā* follows, [the suffix] *tva* is added to *aruṣ*, *uccaiḥ*, *aruh*, and *druh*; [the suffix] *ruha* is added to *cāru*;
*kruṣṭa* is added to *cakruṣ*; and *kruṅ* is added to *amukṣat* and *addha*, when followed by a vowel.
After the word *pa-ha-ṇā-ma-ta*, and also when preceded by *abhi-mitra*, [the following rules apply]:
*drupadaṃ* indeed, *dru*, *dhruvā*, *adhruṅ*, and disregarding *nānā*, there is the *dṛti-śruti*. || 17 ||
Disregarding the stones for the sake of being seen, you were gazed upon; repeatedly lifted up, O God, you are the one who has been praised here with the call, "Bow down to me! Praise me! 18.
May your strength be manifest, O seeker of light; let my fervor not remain in my heart alone.
O you who are heard from the east and above, hear me with readiness; O you whose beard is famous, listen as one who has truly heard! 19.
Duality, the seasons, and sacrifice—these rested upon the ancient *ṛvataḥ*; the path of circumambulation, the upward flow, the stream, and the flowing sound [all followed]. || 20 ||
In the word *sruk*, there is the syllable *sru*; that which possesses the *ṛ* sound (*sasṛvān*) is not found [there].
*Ṣānta* is *pruṭ*; *srukti* is above; and *vāgbhrū*, *śubhru*, and *śatru* [are also above]. || 21 ||

The earth, the eyebrows, the fist, the sky, the deer, and the roar—these [words] have been uttered; and the statement "a hundred enemies" and "me, us"—this is said to be the former state of *nīd*. (22)

One offers with *juhvatyapi* and *āhi juhve*; the last [syllable] is *svāra*. One takes [the portion] with *upabhottare*, provided that the word *juhva* contains the vowel *u* and there is no conjunction [of consonants] following it. (23)

He indeed bestows the will of the gods upon the sacrificers; therefore, he sprinkles [the oblation] for the sake of all beings, and thus he is the all-pervading one who transcends even the highest gods.
The vowel *ṛ* is that which is taken away by rain; he for whom this *ṛ* is successful attains prosperity.
That vowel which ends in the syllable *ṛ* should be known as such by the discerning. (25)
In the word *kḷpta*, the accent is cited as being on the first syllable; it does not occur at the end of a word or a pada.
In *baddhainasā* and *bhavemaicca*, the accent falls on the final syllable; in *yenta*, it occurs on the eleventh and third syllables respectively.
The first [mantra], "juṣetām" (may they enjoy), is for the two [deities] Añjan and Satyau;
the mantra "ye keśinaḥ sa aikāraḥ" (those with long hair, together with the sound 'ai') is described in this context [with the words] "vyaicchan" (they desired). || 27 ||
The Praiyamedhas were like the Nyagrodha and Priyaṅgu trees;
they milked the sacrifice into a tiger-skin vessel, and these [sages] were the Daivāpātyas.
The faculty of the Brahman-varcas, the faculty of cattle, and the faculty of virility follow him;
light from his mouth and strength indeed come to him in this way. || 29 ||
Three [offerings]: to Brahmaṇaspati, to Agni, and to Indra-Agni; and the *purohavis* consists of fat.
These two [oblations] belong to Indra's life-span (*āyuḥ*); at the beginning and at the end, there is an offering to Agni consisting of food (*annavat*).
With the wooden sword (sphyena), [one acts] for the purpose of driving away the heat (gharma) and for the purpose of expelling them.
Hereafter, we shall explain the first letters beginning with *ka*.
They are situated before the semivowels (*antaḥsthā*), the labial class (*pavarga*), and the vowels (*svara*). (31)
The words *triṣṭuk* and *anuṣṭuk* are said to end in the letter *k*;
however, elsewhere it is determined that these two end in the letter *p*.
However, the established rule is that in that case, there is a reversal of the previous injunction. || 33 ||
In *cakṣe*, *su*, *śraddhā*, *ūrdhve*, *kaḥ*, *utkaraḥ*, *antaḥ*, *uccaiḥ*, and *eva kaḥ*; as well as *viṣṭutam*, the word *kṛṣṭa*, and *pacy-ūrdhvaḥ*—but after *ṣa*, it is *ṭa*. (34)
To Tvaṣṭṛ, to Vasu, and to Agni, an eight-potherd cake in the morning;
may Vaiśvānara be pleased; O Mother, may Agni be auspicious to us and may he deliver us. 35.
The Brahman priest indeed delivers this [victim] from those who fall away;
through the oblation, the knower knows this animal as belonging to the Ṛtavyas.
"By means of heat, protect yourself; he protects; protected is the *sāṃhita*.
For the protection of the vital breaths, there are two; for the protection of the worlds, the *brahmaspṛt*. (37)
Sagha, caturtha, node, asisaghyāsaṃ, lānya, megha, ragha, anaghābhyas, āgha, agha, praghāta, and also mogha. || 38 ||
And where there is a word for action, there likewise are *tadanya*, *ghana*, *jaṅgha*, *punastuva*, *pratūrti*, and *tvāvata*; and [perform] the great deed (*bṛhatkṛdhi*). || 39 ||
May he flow forth for us that wealth which we know to be full of vital seed;
the former is the word "Magha" meaning father, while the latter is the term "Maghavan" signifying the possessor of wealth. || 40 ||

"He who desires to kill the three vital breaths and all beings, and he who has already killed them"—it is said that even in the *ṭa*-group [of consonants], one must bear the status of being the fourth, and so forth. (41)
When you cried out while meditating, the earth was divided into four parts; O Brahman, the five final ones were the intellects, the bodies, the splendors, and those who move upwards.
The one who knows the means is the Lord; *jī*, *sī*, *sū*, *dakṣi*, and *mepara*;
*pari*, *syanaḥ*, *punaḥ*, *rdehi*, and the fourth is *vedyūrdhve*. || 43 ||

To whom [belongs] the *svāhā*, whether it be supreme or otherwise, the excellent hearing regarding the ritual act; may Yama not lead us away, nor may the Ordainer [lead us]; from that, the Veda and the mind [arise]. 44.
May Indra, the foremost, grant [this], and may another bestow it upon the descendants of Sukuta in the future;
by that, their lifespan shall be thirty-three years for each of these forms. (45)

The words *śam*, *sam*, *pra*, *ca*, and *na*, as well as *ūrdhva* and *anna* when followed by the word *kāmena*, may also [be elided] even when followed by a word ending in the fourth case; this also applies to those [words] used for the *adhvaryu*.
He gave this sacrificial fee upon the *barhis* grass to the *agnīdh*, the *brahman*, and the *hotṛ*:
a silken garment, gold, and a cow, while he himself was the foremost [of them]. (47)
Because it gives, it possesses a third state; elsewhere it drinks together with that which is the swelling pride, the hunger, and the food itself. 48.

O pure one, you who bestow the power of the senses, grant us that wisdom which is to be meditated upon; O self-reliant one, speak the essence, abandon what is harmful, and be far-reaching among the people. 49.
May there be long-lasting sorrow for me hereafter; may the earth hear the cry of the sinless one.
May the gods grant us a great share, and may we endure together from the very beginning.
Va, ma, da, ba, sa, śa, and ṣa, along with the vowels, are the "cow-pit" (gokura).
These [consonants] beginning with ta and the others, preceded by vowels, as well as those beginning with the letter 'a', are situated below that. (51)
O you who grant wealth to Rādhā, you who have made the depths firm, you who have subdued the wicked,
you who have crushed the hunger of those who struggle, do not abandon me, O sinless one, from this worldly existence.
The subduer of enemies grew great; the piercer, the hearer of battle-calls, and the increaser of the earth were established.
The obstructor was heard, the debt was paid, and the one who was bound was released; the suppliant indeed obtained his desire.
Gavīdhuka, sridha, grodha, idam, adhadhajanadhāḥ, and ṣadha;
even the letter *dh* at the end of a word, as well as rādha, śrud, and avadhiṣma. 54.
Below the chin, he made a loud sound as he was yoked; he also stepped upon the horse's halter. He struck and repelled the quiver.
The *kāyādhva* and the *nidha*, as well as the *nirbādha* and the *abādhiropa*, do not accomplish the *gāudhūma*; such is the established rule regarding the *gāvīdhuka*. || 56 ||

The words *nākāra*, *anta*, *vṛthā*, and *ucca*; *artha* meaning "purpose" and *artha* meaning "wealth"; *tīrtha* and *pārtha*; *vīthī*; *abhāga*; the word *artha*; *rūthya*; and *nirṛtha* [are examples]. (57)
You have conquered, you have struck, you have spread out, you have held fast, and you have driven away.
O Rathītara, they crush the pillar and you scatter them.
You know *vettha*, *āvṛtham*, and *āvṛthāḥ*; you have abandoned [them] with *asthnā* and likewise with *itthā*.
You have raised up *antocakāyi* and *itthau*, both ending in a visarga, provided they are not followed by *śithi*.
And [the suffixes] *thn* and *vidathya* follow after *kati*, *yū*, and *pūrva*. || 60 ||
Śṛṃ, paṃ, graṃ, maṃ, and māṃ are the first; likewise, the fourth is in the Samāna.
Being churned, it is the Rathya-svara, and the earth is also the Rāthantara.
The letter *bha* is said to be other than those [sounds] found in *phala*, *phena*, *phaṇat*, *pharvya*, and *śaphe*;
it is also [found] in *vaiśambhalyā*, at the beginning of *śībhā*, and as the fourth letter in the labial class (*pavarga*).
The word *avāṅ* ends in the letter *ṅ* and always refers to that which is below the navel;
likewise, *yācñā* ends in the letter *ñ* and refers to that which is between the knees.

Why? Because those [consonants] that follow the vowels u, pa, ya, ra, and the nine vowels (a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ, e, o, ai, au), as well as those preceded by ta or followed by ta, are known as *ja* and *ña*, while the others are known as *ga* and *ṅa*. (64)
Many others raised loud shouts of "Unanta! while he stretched out his arms; another, with his face uplifted, reached upward toward the sky.
The word *ātāṃsī* is used for one who praises; *śaṃsin* for one who recites; *āsikya* for a seat; and *duṣad* for an assembly hall.
When there is identity of sound, a nasal (*ṇ*) preceded by *ra*, *ṣ*, or *pa* is substituted [for *na*]; and in some cases, the *v* and *y* are elided after the root *spṛś*.
In *carman*, *carṣaṇ*, *vṛṣan*, *śīrṣan*, *brahman*, *nakṣan*, and *navagraha*;
likewise in *vāṇa*, *śatāṇu*, and *meṇi* etc., the initial *ṇ* is treated as original (*prākṛta*). (67)
The bull, preceded and followed by the *bastas*, [is joined] with the bull; and from the bull comes the state of the bull (*vṛṣṇiya*).
The sacrifice, beginning with the *huk* sound, is Viṣṇu, Kṛṣṇa, as proclaimed in the sequence. (68)
Within it is indeed no end; Indra is not its match, nor does he stand in its midst.
They obstruct the silk garment (tārpya) among these [powers], yet they establish it for the sake of the beyond.
Each one is threefold and belongs to Agni; they all join together for Agni.
For you, O God Indra, are indeed our protector; from the beginning, you have placed us in the higher worlds. 70.
Nine others, the wise Sādhyas, are indeed the six seasons;
they were born from the earth, and it is also said that others stood upon them.
Kusurubindu, Apratiṣṭhā, and Prajāpati—these nine [are the breaths].
Life-force (āyus) is indeed the end; [one attains] Āditya, Prajā, Agni, and that continuity (saṃtati). || 72 ||
From the *dhiṣṇya* [altar], the second [portion] is for the god [Agni] together with the wooden sword (*sphya*) and the *bārha*;
the third and fourth [portions] are for the *brahman*, and one for each individual person.
The gods fall away from one another regarding the deity; such is the rule among them.
Indra is indeed speech, and the threefold sacrificial grass establishes us. || 74 ||
These [waters] flow toward a lack of firm foundation; the *tārpya* garment belongs to the third and fourth [stages].
Whose continuity it is, they join with the *tārpya* garment—the Asurya that reaches the end.
Prajāpati took up the seed; may the cattle prosper us.
These [days] become three upward days; the *pṛṣṭhya* [stoma] does not turn back toward the earth. 76.
The first [verse] belongs to Indra and the bull; it is addressed to Agni, by which he expanded upon this earth.
Indeed, the ancient sages offered the sacrifice; may we be free from disease through the consumption of food.
They will become gods; from them, six and then another six [will arise].
Indra went, and that one went to the gods, but the sense-organ (indriya) did not go.
The *devasya tvā* [formula] and the *sāvitra* [mantra] are said to purify these very [materials];
first, however, one should place them together in the fire without any interval. || 79 ||
O you of great learning, it may be that those various [seasons], even while possessing their own specific deficiencies,
are accomplished by the year as being two-fold, just as the seasons are produced from the sun.
May the Ādityas, Prajāpati, and Aṅgiras, as well as Puruṣa, Dāman, Dyau, and Śakuni, grant us their favor. || 81 ||
Beyond that Brahma-world, the golden realm situated above is remembered here;
it is like the height of many mountains reaching upward even in a level plain. 82.
At the end, Vāruṇa indeed [protects] her with two [verses], and these [Rudras] protect her with seven;
with a Yajus, Agni [protects] her, and Brahmā [protects] her through the long creations.
To Pīvonnā and to Hari, the first-born, we offer salutations;
to Agni, to Dhātṛ and the others, and to the progeny increased on all sides.
In the section on the *muni* (the *yāmi* [verse]), one should also release the *ardhuka*;
having omitted *aitvam*, there is *ṣya* above and *ca* in the middle, with *ya* at one side. (85)
One cuts down while another is being cut down; one is cut off while the other remains.
Indeed, the womb is holy; therefore, from that womb, the embryo is born through great sacrifice.
This great one who exists here, he is indeed the first seasonal priest; O Agni, most youthful one, when you have risen up as the Hotṛ, you are like a harnessed steed.
The mortals of old [recited] "uṣasaṃ" and "amṛtam"; here it is said that [the word] ending in "ā" is "arayiṣṭhā," and [the mantra] "astabhnād dyām" is joined with "da. || 88 ||
The gods settled in the Virāj realm; the year and the seasons were distinct.
Among mortals, Agni was above, while the former [fire] moved upward and forward.
The word *suvarga* has its accent on the final syllable even when followed by the word *loka*;
likewise, for the sake of avoiding nasalization of the *vīrya*, they succeed even in the absence of the letter *r*. (90)

But before the *yuktottama*, when there is identity of sound (*śabdaikya*), there is no nasalization (*anunāsika*). [The syllables] *mano*, *jaya*, and *du*—these five; thirty-three [syllables] following; and the last one is unvoiced (*anudātta*). (91)
Likewise, when the initial syllable is udātta, and when *iṅ* and *ya* are present, there is optionally reduplication here before *gra* and *gar*.
This also applies to *tavya* and *ṣya* even after a long vowel, except when preceded by *medhapati* and *sot*.
And thus, by means of those [syllables], he directly [attains] this husband; likewise, with the mouth, he begins from the front with the *ṛt* (truth) and follows along. 93.
But previously, [the syllable] *agauḥ* [was used] for the sacrifice, the self, and likewise the year;
having grasped the upward [syllable] by means of the sacrifice, one begins from the upward [position] and proceeds to the letter *ra*.
Having won over men, he is unassailable; he is to be scrutinized even by one who is advancing.
The triad beginning with cattle is to be examined; the gods, the Hotṛ-priests, and the letter *ra* are incomparable.
Atapyata, aparaḥ, somaḥ, cādyāḥ, and pañca are more difficult to restrain;
likewise, sūrya, āditya, payodhātā, dūrāt, and api ca sauryaraḥ [are difficult to restrain]. (96)
One offers oblations with loving-kindness, standing upright; the singer stands upright.
Within the middle of the nasal channel, one should dissolve another who is dissolved in the nose. 97.
The *dīrgha* [stoma] and the *prajāvatīrvaśca* [stomas], as well as the *nakṣatra* and the *graha*;
the seven triplets of domestic animals are the *vasu*, and thereafter the *ekavimśati* and the *trivṛt*. 98.
In its own abode, it should be placed in the Stoma as its womb;
for in this case, the subsequent [form] ending in the vowel *ai* is proclaimed by the rule "with its own deity" (*svayā devatayā*). || 99 ||
The words *kaṣa*, *cāṣa*, *jaṣa*, *caṣāla*, *māṣa*, and *vājaka*; the word *ṣāṭ* preceded by a non-ṣ vowel; the word *ṣaṇ*; and the word *nada* with an *ūrdhva* [anusvāra], such as *maṣam*. (100)
He is said here to be the best of friends, established in his station; he who satisfies all these four [qualities], even as a horse that brings about success. || 101 ||

And indeed, those two [fires] are extinguished; "this belongs to these very ones," so it is said. By what is the sacrificial session (satra) concluded? It is not joined with the numbers one, two, or three.
The *chandas*, the gods, the *surās*, by that [means], formerly, rain-bringers, cattle; as they established [them] with endings in the third case, so indeed [are] *mānta* and *vānta*. 103.

When one says, "O Indra, may the sacrifice of my rival be [taken] by the wife and others," and also "by the Yajus and the meters," he deprives his adversary of [the fruit of] the sacrifice; may that sacrifice be fully cooked for oneself.
In the beginning, the gods and asuras spoke thus; likewise, Devaka Draviṇa made all the ages full of light, as it is celebrated.

Once these have been created by him from this [sacrifice], the Supreme Lord does not look upon these animals as mere cattle; for as long as they exist, they perform the sacrifice with their very essence (medas) on the previous day through the mind.
He was afraid of that [soma]; he [the horse] emitted fire from him, and even the horse emitted fire. Yaśas cut away the ṛtukṣu; the earth desired to perform the fire-rite. || 107 ||
He [created] Anujāvara, and furthermore Indra, King Soma, as well as Sṛṣṭāśva, Virāja, Agni, and likewise Puruṣa.
In that [section] it is proclaimed: "He [is] Indra, the supreme god, and the asuras";
and in this [section], "He created him from this," likewise in the subsequent Aśvamedha.
The Agnihotra is the highest among sacrifices; the gods are beyond it by means of evil;
Viśvakarman is above that; and the Vyāna breath is the middle, being further beyond by means of the solar ray (aṃśu).
"Neither *kaḥ* nor *tvā* [should be used] in a sentence that is like a *grantha*; nor [should they be used] in a single-sentence formula containing *svāhā* or *ūrdhva*.
One's offspring would become more prosperous through the *trivṛt*; however, the former [verse] itself is superior. (111)
Savitṛ placed the Hotṛ priest Pradaśa at the beginning of the twelve Asuras;
he placed Ānyā at the beginning of that [group], and Ambhāṃsi between the two.
The second and third [syllables] are preceded by fire (Agni), and likewise the next pair;
as many as there are in the first, so are they in the fourth; and that which is with one [syllable] applies to the first triad.
The earth and the first two [elements] exist both here and there, and thus everywhere;
but the last is light or water, or these very same things.
Prajāpati indeed leads away the Rākṣasas from these [beings];
at the beginning, he leads them along with their wealth, and he joins them together according to their kind.
"O Darbha, may this non-Brahmin depart from here;
[he is] like you, situated in the midst of three things similar to horses. (116)
The second [verse] is for those who have moved; one should offer the supreme oblation.
"Let him partake," "O slayer," "threefold," "Nandā," "you must summon," and "he bestows in the direction. || 117 ||
May the excellent [goddess] whose vowels end in *i* and who consists of the letter *ra* in sequence, as well as those others who are otherwise arranged, being auspicious, grant what is dear. 118.
The Earth spoke aloud, having been made manifest by clarified butter:
"O Night and Day, O Moon, you shall not find a new womb beyond this. 119.
By this it has been stated: "The sacrificial animal belongs to Agni; do not investigate otherwise. The immortal breath is the Sun; follow the one who moves along with the body. (120)
Therefore, speak thus to him: "For you are a guest who has come among your kinsmen;
may they welcome you with offerings, and may both of you live together in splendor. (121)
They did not desire the sacrificial cake; the quarters [of the world] and our difficult task were [established].
O Viṣṇu, you have propped up and supported [the earth], while they strike down as I go and come.
May the fierce and sharp [weapon] of Hanidhin crush him to pieces;
moreover, let it consume him who steals or consumes what has been entrusted to him. 123.
The covering of the two-fold poison and the like is Rohit; Rohit is upright, the sacrificer is the support.
"May the directions be praised for us, so that the auspicious one may grant prosperity;
the makers of the clarified butter have spoken aloud: 'For the earth, we have proclaimed you.'"
Whether it be night or day, or whether the moon shall rise, you shall not approach our womb;
therefore, speak this to him, for he is a guest come to us, O kinsmen.
These other sacrificial animals of his are not like that;
they are connected with the lower nectar, the Adityas, and the Tanūnapāt, following the Anuṣṭubh.
May they enjoy the living beings born from the lotuses;
do not strike me here with a sharp and crushing weapon.

O Viṣṇu, you have propped up and firmly established [the world]; those who strike me down and those who go away—may they consume the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa); you are the covering, difficult to overcome.
May they protect him, or let him study; from this fruit may they be bestowed upon him. May they endow him with splendor, and may he be free from seizure.
"Beyond [the vowel], one should not be despondent; shine with the subtle [vowels] and grow.
One should obtain [them] from Savitṛ, for with the head we [attain] blessings.
Thus, there are two visargas in the middle, and *u* is at the end. 124.
"O gods, this is Indra; indeed, Indra by his signal has overcome the Vṛtras;
or that which is this Pavamāna—this is the third," so it is also said. (125)
In the second [section], however, it is indeed "pradevaṃ hi devīḥ," "prācīna," and "caiva cet"; likewise, "samiddho agniḥ" and "saṃkrūraṃ suvardākṣi," and not otherwise. || 126 ||
The *vaṣaṭkāra* is the reverse; indeed, for Agni Vaiśvānara it is *parā*.
For the deity, [the formulas] beginning with *ahaṃ* and all those ending with *vayaḥ* destroy the others nine times. (127)
The eleventh is the Agniṣṭoma; what indeed is this Brahmā? He is truly all-pervading.
Vāstoṣpati and Indra are invited, as is the Hotṛ priest and Agni first.
The threefold truth of Prajāpati, O Deva Savitṛ, and the sacrifice itself—this they say is successfully accomplished when led; for that is indeed the all-encompassing and the heavenly world.

Furthermore, these same *chandases* [metres] belong to them, with the exception of those for water and the last one even among the animals; these are the *devikās*, and they are indeed established as such through the *sampannā*. 130.
The *samidhs* are before the self; the *dāvidhṛti* is the ear; by them [the sacrifice is] most excellent.
You are that at the end; this [sacrifice] is in me; you are all, and you are the firm foundation (*dhruva*). || 131 ||
Whatever kind of sound occurs in a given position has been thus proclaimed;
the phonemes should be understood by the wise according to their case endings, genders, and forms. (132)

The sequence, the movement, the explicit statement, the two words beginning with "yajus," the number of words, the number of syllables, and the eight points of attention—these are [to be known] by the wise. (133)
He who understands the Bharadvāja-śikṣā along with its meaning attains the world of Brahmā, just as a householder reaches his home. 134.
The Bhāradvājaśikṣā is completed.
